affected_predicate.description: An email with Emily_Anderson_CV.pdf attached and subject candidates_cv is sent to HR_chen@gmail.com.

competing_trace_defects.description: The trajectory repeatedly tapped the resume row while the Downloads view remained effectively unchanged, without opening or sharing the file, before abandoning that approach for the Mail app.
Recipient and subject text were entered without first focusing their fields; the compose screen remained blank, and the subsequent send attempt produced a missing-recipient alert.

chains.rationale: At step 24, the reused false send claim supported another click on Send while the recipient and subject fields were visibly empty. The resulting missing-recipient alert shows preservation of the false-completion defect. After dismissing the alert, steps 26-29 explicitly focus and populate the recipient and subject while retaining the visible attachment. Step 30 then invokes Send and returns to the inbox, visibly correcting the harmful mechanism and supporting the affected predicate.

summary: The single strict-MHR chain visibly repeats a send attempt under the false premise that required email fields were already populated. The repeated attempt triggers the same missing-recipient alert, after which the trajectory corrects the recipient and subject fields and performs a send that returns to the inbox. Independent earlier defects include an unproductive file-row tapping loop and unfocused text entry into the compose form.
